title: Choose landing spots with rays from the open sky, and measure every site
observation: Automatic landing spots near each island's treasure were chosen by downward raycasts. Probing from just above the treasure's height accepted ground under a cave roof (Crystal Isle's treasure is inside a spire), and the throw hit the hillside. Probing from 900 studs up rejected anything under a roof or overhang. A fix checked on three islands passed; measuring all sixteen found two more islands that needed their own handling (a cave and a crater rim), and treasures under a roof needed a designer-given hint for where to aim.
recommendation: Start placement rays from above the highest geometry so covered ground is rejected, require clear ground all round the spot, and measure the real path on every site rather than a sample.
applies_when: Generating spawn, landing or drop points from raycasts
Validating a placement rule across many hand-built sites
limits: One archipelago of 16 islands, measured on one Studio client

evidence.detail: The V12 chapter, Landing where you picked: the rule as built.
